## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ea0729835c1b26f316b7598294ec4a99d842ca5c`
Local-runs: probe — one node run of the pure `addOnlyNoteReasons` (the `scripts/` tree of 1d110f52 extracted by `git archive` into a scratch folder, 17 hand-built patches), because a FAIL on a governance boundary should rest on what the reader returns, not on my reading of its regexes. `git diff 1d110f52 ea072983` is three self-test fixture strings (ADR-0200 to ADR-0154: two in check-governed-merges.mjs, one in check-governed-queue-guard.mjs), so the reader that ran is byte-identical on this head. Nothing built, no self-test or gate re-run.
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md, AGENTS.md + scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs, scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs, scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs

### ① Derived judgments

- Net diff against `main` (merge base 895783a1): 5 files, +578 −42, the five the claim 6895962078 and its amendment 6896182750 name. Nothing outside the claimed surface.
- Check-runs on this head are NOT a verdict yet: 1 success, 4 skipped, 14 in progress when read (every Lint and Type Check leg, Check PR Size, PR-body guards). On the previous head 1d110f52, `Lint · repo & tooling gates` and its roll-up `Lint & Repo Gates` were red: `check-adr-anchors --self-test` refused the fixtures' `ADR-0200` as a citation of a record that does not exist. This head's one commit answers exactly that; whether it is green is still pending.
- The dev report 6896690587 names head 1d110f52 and says 53 of 53 gates ran with 0 failed. `check:adr-anchors` was red on that head in CI, so that count did not hold for it. The report is one head stale.
- The arm's conditions are reused, not re-spelled: the ADR leg runs inside `lowRiskArmVerdict` behind the same body, label, timeline, fork, security-name, status and mode checks. The register row keeps `tier: H` and gains `lowRisk: { repos: ['objectstack'], addOnly: true }`.
- Line budgets hold: AGENTS.md 1050 to 1050, SKILL.md 320 to 320, the `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**` family 3236 to 3236. No issue number on any added line of AGENTS.md or the skill.

### ② Semver level

None. No published package is touched: scripts, AGENTS.md and an internal skill only. `skip-changeset` is on the PR and is right. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are on the body and are right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, head in the base repository (no fork), still draft. The diff moves the governed register and AGENTS.md, so the PR itself is Tier H and the maintainer merges it. No seat approval is implied by this record.
- Dev open question (assignee and reviewers not set): answered. The owning seat requests both `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` when it readies the PR; nothing for the dev to do.
- Deviation, surface amendment for execute.mjs: recorded in 6896182750 before the push, and the tree matches it. All five hunks sit inside `selfTest()`; no relay logic changed.
- Deviation, the dev session model: not material to this record, which is an independent review.
- Deviation, `pnpm lint` not run: answered by the Lint legs on this head, still pending.
- SQL push-down: n/a.

### ④ Design judgment

The probe's two controls behaved: a plain appended note section passes, an appended `## Decision` is refused. Everything below was appended to or inserted in the self-test's own `RECORD` and PASSED as an add-only note unless it says otherwise.

M1 (must-fix) — a real `## Decision` heading passes when a quoted fence sits above it. Three added lines (a quote marker followed by a three-backtick fence opener; `## Decision`; `We now allow X.`) at the end of the record return no reason. `addOnlyHeadingReading` strips quote markers and keeps one file-wide `fence` state, so it reads the heading as code. In CommonMark the fence belongs to the block quote and ends with it; the next unquoted line is a top-level H2. This is the card's own named H case ("no added line … sits under a `Decision` heading"), landed with a seat's PASS and no maintainer.

M2 (must-fix) — a `Decision` heading inside a list item passes in three spellings: (a) a hyphen, a TAB, then `## Decision`; (b) `- - ## Decision`; (c) `- > ## Decision`. `unquote` strips one list marker, only when followed by spaces and `#`. Each renders as a Decision heading with the new text under it.

M3 (must-fix) — a `Decision` heading split by an inline construct the normaliser does not strip passes: `## De[](#)cision` (an empty link) and the same heading with an empty bold element (open tag, close tag) between `De` and `cision`. `addOnlyHeadingText` removes only `*_`~` and default-ignorable characters. Both render as "Decision".

The three share a cause, and fixing the six strings one by one will not close it: the reader is a denylist over Markdown and each round has found more shapes (this is the fourth). The file's own note on `LOW_RISK_RIDER_PATTERNS` says a denylist fails open. An allowlist for what an added run may contain (blank lines, one plain ATX heading that is not ruled, plain or `> ` quoted prose with no fence marker, no list-borne `#`, no left angle bracket, no empty link) would refuse everything it does not recognise. Each of the shapes above needs a self-test row either way.

S1 (should-fix) — raw HTML is refused only at the start of a line or as a comment. `Note` followed by an unclosed strikethrough tag (the one-letter `s` element), inserted under Context, passes, and an unclosed formatting tag can strike through the Decision text below it in a renderer; `Text` followed by an inline level-2 HTML heading element reading Decision passes too. The reason text and the PR body both say an added line carries no raw HTML; the tree does not hold that.

S2 (should-fix) — status lines are read in English and with a narrow tail. `**状态**:已被 ADR-0200 取代` passes, although the ruled-heading test reads 状态. `Status (2026-11-15): Superseded by ADR-0200` passes because a parenthesis sits between the word and the colon. The fullwidth colon is caught.

N1 (nit) — a link reference definition inside a list item (`- [a]: https://…`) passes; the bare spelling is refused. It can retarget an existing reference link.

N2 (nit) — on the earlier head the fixtures cited an unwritten ADR number; fixed here.

What held under attack, read in the code: a whitespace-only change or a moved line shows as a removal (H); renames are read with `--no-renames` and any added, deleted or renamed row is H; a binary diff, a mode change, a symlink, several hunks, a hunk not at line 1 and mismatched counts are H; an unread diff is H at `--pr`, the relay and the queue; a new file, a non-`.md` file, `README.md` and a subfolder under `docs/adr/` are H; any other governed row beside the ADR (AGENTS.md, NORTH-STAR) and any path outside the rider allowlist are H; the read is merge base to head, so a base far behind `main` adds nothing from `main`, and the queue leg reads each queued commit against its first parent; an added fence, frontmatter or heading that re-scopes existing lines is H; headings indented four spaces under a list are over-read as headings (H, fail closed); additions in the header block, where the registry keeps `**Status**:`, are H in any spelling.

AGENTS.md Prime Directive 14: the wording ("skills-only wording and add-only ADR notes (`lowRiskArmVerdict` …) read as S") matches the register row. It is true only as far as the reader is; with M1 to M3 open, "add-only ADR notes" admits a Decision heading. The cut clause ("the post-merge audit is the compensating control") keeps its home at lines 305 to 307 of the same directive ("Behind it: … the post-merge audit … lists every governed-surface merge"). Acceptable.

SKILL.md: line 204 names the ADR leg truthfully. The `.github/workflows/**` glob survives at line 184. "(该面独占)" for "(技能独占)" is no worse than before. Ratchet flat, no issue numbers.

check-governed-queue-guard.mjs: `catalogFilesOf` asks for the same argv through `addOnlyDiffArgv` and carries a failed read as `null`, which the arm reads H. It agrees with the register; it inherits M1 to M3 because it calls the same reader.

execute.mjs: fixtures only. The moved fixtures keep their pins on a Tier H row outside the arm, and the new row pins that an ADR path beside `packages/core` reads the arm and still plans Tier H with both approvers.

Three must-fix, two should-fix, two nits.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d038e0dea4628b22000b865534f5d75bb010fdf5`
Local-runs: probe — one node run of the pure `addOnlyNoteReasons` and `addOnlyHeadingReading` from this head (`scripts/` and `docs/adr/` extracted by `git archive` into a scratch folder, since deleted): 41 hand-built patches plus one appended plain note over each of the 155 shipped records. The delta round asks for the pass rows and the corpus claim to be confirmed on the code, and a governance reader is judged on what it returns. Nothing built, no self-test or gate re-run.
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md, AGENTS.md + scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs, scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs, scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs

### ① Derived judgments

- Delta `ea072983..d038e0de` is one commit on one file, scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs (+75 −31): the allowlist constants, the quote-scoped fence in `addOnlyHeadingReading`, the unmodelled-record refusal, and the self-test rows. The other four files are byte-identical to the head record 6896800633 judged.
- Net diff against `main` (merge base 895783a1): the same 5 claimed files, +622 −42. The dev report 6897071708 still says 578 additions; the number is stale, the file list is right.
- Check-runs on this head: 26 success, 22 skipped, none pending, none red. `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards` and the `Lint & Repo Gates` roll-up are green. The red `check:adr-anchors` of 1d110f52 is gone.
- Line budgets unchanged: AGENTS.md 1050, SKILL.md 320.
- Corpus claim confirmed by the probe: an appended plain note section reads S on 149 of 155 shipped records. The 6 that read H (0001, 0043, 0046, 0051, 0084, 0107) all give one reason, no decision or status heading. The reader is not fail-closed into uselessness.

### ② Semver level

None. No published package is touched. `skip-changeset` is on the PR and is right; `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are on the body and are right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, no fork, still draft. The PR moves the governed register and AGENTS.md, so it is Tier H and the maintainer merges it. This record is the seat's review of record, not an approval.
- Dev open questions: none in 6897071708. The earlier one (assignee and reviewers) stays answered: the owning seat requests both `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` at ready.
- Deviation, two of the dev's own pass rows changed direction (a balanced code block added in Context, and a heading with emphasis, now read H): accepted. Both are the allowlist failing closed, and both rows are renamed to say so.
- Deviation, `gh api` used for two reads: no write, not material.
- Deviation, `pnpm lint` not run by the dev: answered, `Lint · ESLint` is green on this head.
- execute.mjs surface amendment: unchanged since 6896800633, self-test only.
- SQL push-down: n/a.

### ④ Design judgment

Findings of record 6896800633, each re-run on this head with the string that record gave:

- M1: closed — a quoted fence opener above an unquoted `## Decision` reads H, twice over: the fence marker is off the allowlist, and the reader now ends a quoted fence when the quote ends, so the heading is read as a heading.
- M2: closed — the tab-bullet, double-bullet and bullet-then-quote spellings all read H. A line starting `#` must be a plain column-0 heading, and prose behind a marker must start on a letter, digit, quote or bracket.
- M3: closed — the empty-link and empty-element headings read H. Heading text is letters, digits, spaces and plain punctuation only.
- S1: closed — a left angle bracket anywhere on an added line reads H.
- S2: closed — the Chinese status line and the dated `Status (…):` line read H. A fullwidth, upper-case spelling does too.
- N1: closed — a link reference definition reads H bare, quoted and behind a list marker.
- N2: closed on ea072983.

The allowlist under attack. Refused (H), all confirmed by the run: fullwidth number signs as a heading; a zero-width character in a heading; an added `===` or `---` underline below an added line; an added line above an existing thematic break (it re-scopes existing lines, and names a ruled heading if it says Decision); a lazy quote followed by `## Decision`; a level-1 `# Decision`; a heading indented one space or behind a two-space quote; a line starting with a curly bracket; a table header with its delimiter row. A digit-and-dot start passes only as a one-level ordered list item, which re-scopes nothing. The five plain-note rows pass: a quoted note under a new section, a list with a link and code, a Chinese note, prose in Context, and a new section between Decision and Consequences.

Two shapes still pass that should not:

S3 (should-fix) — a prose line added directly above an existing setext heading joins that heading. On a record whose ruled heading is `Decision` over a dash underline, adding `No longer the` on the line above passes, and the heading renders as "No longer the Decision". The reader takes only the last line above the underline as the heading text, so it sees no change. No shipped record has a setext decision or status heading today (0 of 155), so this is latent, and a new record lands at Tier H. The fix is small: refuse a run whose next existing line is a setext heading's text.

S4 (should-fix) — the plain-heading letter class is every Unicode letter, so a heading spelled wholly in look-alike letters from other scripts (Cyrillic and Armenian, no Latin letter for the mixed-script test to catch) passes and renders as "decision". A letter-spaced `## D e c i s i o n` passes too. Neither is the word at text level, so search and a model reviewer see the difference; a person reading the rendered page does not. Restricting heading letters to ASCII and Han, and testing the ruled words with spaces and punctuation removed, closes both.

Nits, none affecting the contract:

- N3 (nit) — a status word behind an allowed opener passes: `(Status): Superseded …`, a double-quoted `Status`, and `Current status: …`. The status test is a spelling list and cannot be completed; the header block, where the registry keeps the status, refuses every addition.
- N4 (nit) — a bold `**Decision**` line and a mid-line image pass as prose. They are not headings. What a note says is for the same-head review to read, not this reader.
- N5 (nit) — an unclosed `~~` on an added line passes; it can only reach text in the same paragraph, outside a ruled section.
- N6 (nit) — the dev report's `diff.additions` is one head stale.

Why S3 and S4 do not fail the round: the three must-fix findings were real Markdown headings carrying the word Decision that the reader did not see. That class is closed, and it is closed by construction rather than by string. What remains needs either a record shape the registry does not have, or deliberate look-alike lettering that is not the ruled word. Both should be fixed in a follow-up card; neither changes existing decision text or puts a line under a heading the reader recognises as ruled.

AGENTS.md Prime Directive 14 and SKILL.md line 204: unchanged since the last record, and now truthful as written. "Add-only ADR notes" is what `lowRiskArmVerdict` admits. The cut "compensating control" clause keeps its home in the same directive's "Behind it:" sentence.

check-governed-merges.mjs: the register row, the argv, the hunk parser and the arm's shared conditions are unchanged. The added-line rule is now an allowlist plus the earlier position and heading checks, which is the stance the file already takes for rider paths. The unmodelled-record refusal (a list-borne or indented fence, a raw HTML block) fails closed on the record rather than guessing.

check-governed-queue-guard.mjs and execute.mjs: unchanged; both read through the same reader and inherit the fix.

No must-fix. Two should-fix (S3, S4) for a follow-up card, four nits.
